$description: contrast: more. A.1.6 scopes this to colour only. Nothing publishes high-contrast values for a twelve-step ramp, so this introduces no colour: it moves which step each role resolves to, one rung further from the surface it sits on, which is the practice the ramp's own source documents. Every value reached here already exists in base.grey, so the theme modifier composes with it — resolving contrast after theme means `more` picks a further step of whichever ramp theme chose.

raised.$description: Step 04 rather than 03, so a raised surface separates further from the base it sits on.

fill.$description: Only the subtle rungs move. A subtle fill is constrained against the surface beneath it, so a step away from that surface improves it. A solid fill is constrained against its own ink, which sits at the far end of the ramp, so every step away from the surface is a step toward the ink: at step 11 `sys.color.on.fill` measures 1.8:1 and Lc 34, below the non-text floor, and the context meant to raise contrast would have lowered it. Steps 09 and 10 already clear every floor that applies to them — 3.81:1 and 4.77:1 against the page, Lc 68.6 and Lc 61.3 against the ink — so there is nothing here for this context to fix.

subtle.$description: Step 04 rather than 03, so a control at rest separates further from the surface under it.

subtle-strong.$description: Step 05 rather than 04, keeping the engaged rung one step above the resting one.

muted.$description: Step 12 rather than 11. Secondary text stops being secondary by tone, which is the trade this context exists to make: at normal contrast step 11 reaches APCA Lc 60.5 and clears only the secondary floor, and step 12 reaches Lc 95.4 and clears the body floor.

component-strong.$description: Step 09 rather than 08, which is where this context steps outside A.2.2's border scale: without it the engaged rung would resolve to the same step as the resting one and the ladder would lose a rung in the context meant to sharpen it.
